A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 15-page versions of the same SRA paper. Text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison; thirteen pages render identically.

before.justification: Sections 4–5 and Appendix C report original distillation experiments, benchmark scores, automatic response evaluations, efficiency measurements, and ablation results.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, including the main benchmark comparisons and supplementary experiments in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix D retain identical span alignment, attention-weighted pooling, geometric regularization, span-level logit distillation, and training objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions train on Databricks-Dolly-15k and evaluate on Dolly, VicunaEval, SelfInst, S-NI, and DialogSum. The cross-tokenizer and shared-tokenizer scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within the main benchmark, shared-tokenizer, and supplementary comparisons. This includes the ALM comparison in Table 13 and CDM's participation in the efficiency comparison in Table 5.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix B retain the same preprocessing, teacher–student configurations, training settings, and ROUGE-L evaluation. The GPT-4o-mini judging procedure and Appendix E prompt also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The loss-component and weighting ablations in Tables 2–3, sharpness and transferred-layer analyses in Tables 10–11, and logit-loss ablation in Table 12 are identical. The vocabulary-overlap analysis is also unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions state that evaluation results are averaged over five random seeds in Section 4.1. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All benchmark scores, judging win rates, efficiency measurements, and ablation findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains SRA's average ROUGE-L of 17.97 for Qwen1.5–1.8B to GPT-2 120M and 18.10 for the corresponding GPT-2 340M student.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and loss equations are identical, as are Appendix A's hierarchical center-of-mass derivation and Transformer analogy.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about span-based distillation, its physical motivation, and performance relative to existing distillation methods.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and mechanism explanations are unchanged. Section 7 retains the same limitations concerning computational budgets, static logit mapping, storage requirements, and on-the-fly teacher inference.

D1.justification: Training configurations and hyperparameters in Appendix B, hardware and timing details in Table 5, Appendix D pseudocode, and Appendix E evaluation prompt are unchanged. No technical or code/data access disclosure is added or removed.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works, the reference list, and the paper's positioning relative to earlier research are unchanged.

P1.justification: The acknowledgment changes from project support under AFOSR award FA9550-23-S-0001 to support for Trung Le under AFOSR award FA2386-25-1-4023 and ARC grant DP250100262. The arXiv version/date stamp also updates; scientific prose and document structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The longer acknowledgment causes small spacing and text-reflow adjustments in the right column of page 9. All figures, tables, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 revises funding attribution and grant identifiers, updates the version stamp, and slightly adjusts local spacing. The methods, empirical evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and limitations are identical, leaving overall paper quality effectively unchanged.
